
'''Ōkunitama Shrine / Ōkunitama Shrine''' (おおくにたまじんじゃ) is the name used for certain Shinto shrines, rendered either as "大国魂神社" or "大國魂神社", and also sometimes written as "大国霊神社" or "大国玉神社". Below is an explanation of the differences in the kanji spellings followed by a list of the major shrines under each spelling.

== Spelled as "大国魂神社" ==
This form uses the simplified character 国 in place of the traditional 國. It is the form commonly used in modern contexts.
* [[会津大国魂神社|Aizu Ōkunitama Shrine]] – located in [[Fukushima Prefecture]], [[Ōnuma District]], [[Aizumisato]], Miyabayashi: a subsidiary shrine within the precincts of [[伊佐須美神社|Isasumi Shrine]].
* [[大国魂神社 (堺市堺区)|Ōkunitama Shrine (Sakai City, Sakai Ward)]] – located in [[Osaka Prefecture]], [[Sakai]], [[Sakai-ku, Sakai|Sakai Ward]], 甲斐町東: a subsidiary shrine within the precincts of [[開口神社|Aguchi Shrine]].

=== Branches of [[Ōyamato Shrine]] ===
* [[大和大国魂神社|Yamato Okunitama Shrine, Minamiawaji]] – located in [[Hyōgo Prefecture]], [[Minamiawaji|Minamiawaji City]], Enokiretsu.
* [[倭大国魂神社|Yamato Okunitama Shrine, Mima]] – located in [[Tokushima Prefecture]], [[Mima, Tokushima|Mima City]], 美馬町, Shigekiyo.

== Spelled as "大國魂神社" ==
This form retains the traditional character 國 and is often used by shrines that emphasize historical prestige or formality.
* [[大國魂神社 (いわき市)|Ōkunitama Shrine (Iwaki)]] – located in [[Fukushima Prefecture]], [[Iwaki, Fukushima|Iwaki City]], Hirasuganami.
* [[Ōkunitama Shrine]] – located in [[Tokyo|Tokyo Metropolis]], [[Fuchū, Tokyo|Fuchū City]], 宮町: the head shrine (総社) of [[Musashi Province]], hosting the annual grand festival くらやみ祭.
* [[島大國魂神社|Shima Ōkunitama Shrine]] – located in [[Nagasaki Prefecture]], [[Tsushima, Nagasaki|Tsushima City]], Kamitsushima Town.

== Spelled as "大国霊神社" ==
This variant uses the character 霊 (rei) instead of 魂 (tama). The reading may be "Ōkunitama Jinja" or "Ōkunirei Jinja".
* [[Owari Ōkunitama Shrine]] – located in [[Aichi Prefecture]], [[Inazawa|Inazawa City]], 国府宮: also known as Kokufumiya Shrine.

== Spelled as "大国玉神社" ==
This variant employs the character 玉 (tama) to denote sacred treasures. It is usually rendered in the simplified form "大国玉神社", though in some cases the traditional form "大國玉神社" is used.
* [[大国玉神社 (桜川市)|Okunitama Shrine]] – located in [[Ibaraki Prefecture]], [[Sakuragawa, Ibaraki|Sakuragawa City]], Ogunitama: also referred to as 大國玉神社.
* [[大国玉神社 (松阪市)|Ōkunitama Shrine (Matsusaka)]] – located in [[Mie Prefecture]], [[Matsusaka|Matsusaka City]], Rokkon Town.
* [[大國玉神社 (壱岐市)|Ōkunitama Shrine (Iki)]] – located in [[Nagasaki Prefecture]], [[Iki, Nagasaki|Iki City]], Gounoura Town.
